review_notes: I read the whole 37-line file. It has one theorem and no new top-level definitions. Inside the proof it builds an AddSubgroup by hand with carrier fixedPoints (F ∘ F). I checked Mathlib for an existing subgroup of the points where two homomorphisms agree. AddMonoidHom.eqLocus (to_additive of MonoidHom.eqLocus) in Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Ker.lean has membership iff f x = g x. I have not compiled the replacement. The case is modest because the subgroup is only a local `let`, not a public declaration. I treated the rest of the proof (Finite H, card_nsmul_eq_zero') as normal Mathlib use.

findings.problem: The proof hand-builds an AddSubgroup whose elements are the x with F (F x) = x, proving add_mem', zero_mem' and neg_mem' one by one. This is the equaliser of the additive homomorphisms F.comp F and AddMonoidHom.id M. Mathlib already has that as AddMonoidHom.eqLocus, a subgroup with simp lemma mem_eqLocus (x ∈ f.eqLocus g ↔ f x = g x). The local construction repeats that closure API, and it is why the proof needs `change` to convert between fixed-point membership and F (F a₁) = a₁.
findings.proposed_change: Use `let H : AddSubgroup M := AddMonoidHom.eqLocus (F.comp F) (AddMonoidHom.id M)`, or `AddMonoidHom.eqLocus (F.comp F) (.id M)`. Delete the three closure proofs. Membership is then definitionally F (F x) = x, and `AddMonoidHom.mem_eqLocus` handles the conversions. For the finiteness hypothesis, `hfin` is about the set Function.fixedPoints (F ∘ F), which should be defeq to the carrier {x | (F.comp F) x = x}. If it is not accepted directly, a small `Set.Finite` conversion is enough.
findings.benefit: The proof gets shorter and uses the standard Mathlib subgroup, so readers do not have to re-verify the closure properties. It also fits other eqLocus/ker lemmas.
